data.description:
## Story

As a developer, the arbiter output is enriched with three enum-array fields (`cross_reviewer_agreement`, `cross_cycle_pattern`, `impact_class`) and the BLOCK gate enforces an 8-category `impact_class` floor, so that the arbiter is the intelligent cross-cycle decision-maker designed in brainstorm (not a simple severity rule engine) and SC1 + SC6 are satisfied.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] Define enum vocabulary for `cross_reviewer_agreement` (4 values): `UNANIMOUS` (all reviewers flagged), `MAJORITY` (>50%), `SPLIT` (= 50% or even split), `SINGLE_REVIEWER` (only one). Documented in code-reviewer-arbiter.md.
- [ ] Define enum vocabulary for `cross_cycle_pattern` (7 values): `NEW_INTRODUCED` (first appearance), `RECURRING` (in cycle K and K-1), `RESUSTAIN_OF` (in cycle K and prior, was defended), `RESOLVED_THEN_REINTRODUCED` (gone in K-1, back in K), `ESCALATED` (severity rose since prior cycle), `DEFENDED_PRIOR_CYCLE` (had accepted defense in prior cycle), `UNKNOWN` (ledger gap prevents classification). Documented in code-reviewer-arbiter.md.
- [ ] Define enum vocabulary for `impact_class` (8 values, per SC6): `bug`, `unintended_behavior`, `security_vulnerability`, `data_loss_or_corruption`, `secret_exposure`, `compliance_violation`, `api_contract_break`, `infrastructure_break`. Plus a special non-floor value `none` for findings outside the floor. Documented in code-reviewer-arbiter.md.
- [ ] Update `code-reviewer-arbiter.md` agent prompt: each output ruling MUST include all three array/enum fields. `cross_reviewer_agreement` and `cross_cycle_pattern` are JSON arrays (allow multiple values when applicable, e.g., RECURRING + DEFENDED_PRIOR_CYCLE). `impact_class` is a single enum value. Agent prompt includes guidance on how to derive each field from the input bundle.
- [ ] Update `validate_cycle_end_ruling` in arbiter.py to enforce enum membership: cross_reviewer_agreement values ∈ 4-set, cross_cycle_pattern values ∈ 7-set, impact_class ∈ 9-set (8 floor + 'none'). Raise ValueError on unknown enum values. Backward-compat: missing fields raise ValueError (new schema requires them).
- [ ] Extend BLOCK-gate AND-logic in code-reviewer-arbiter.md and in any enforcement code: BLOCK requires severity ∈ {critical, important} AND defense rejected/absent AND cycle_num ≤ max_cycles AND `impact_class` ∈ 8-category floor (impact_class='none' MUST NOT BLOCK regardless of severity).
- [ ] Extend arbiter input bundle to include per-reviewer-agent breakdown of which reviewer flagged each finding (needed for cross_reviewer_agreement computation) and a reference to or excerpt of cycle ledger history (needed for cross_cycle_pattern). dispatch_arbiter signature updated; runner.py/local orchestrator pass the additional inputs.
- [ ] Update all 7 fixtures in tests/fixtures/arbiter/ to include the new fields. Test `validate_cycle_end_ruling` rejects fixtures with hallucinated enum values. Test BLOCK fixture with impact_class='none' is reclassified to DEFER.
- [ ] schema_version bumped 1.0.0 → 1.1.0; contracts/review-defenses.md arbiter sub-schema updated.

## Considerations

- [Scope] Bumps schema to 1.1.0. Defense store readers are forward-compat (S6) so existing records continue to load.
- [BLOCK floor edge case] A critical-severity finding with impact_class='none' becomes DEFER (not BLOCK), preventing over-blocking of theoretical-only issues. Fixture added for this case.
- [Arbiter input plumbing] This story requires changes to how reviewer outputs are bundled. Coordinate with Story 13 (CI runner.py wiring) and Story 14 (local wiring) for input shape consistency.
- [Ordering] Depends on Story 10 (uses cycle_ledger for pattern computation input).
- [Independent of 11] Story 12 can implement schema independently of Story 11's processor; Stories 13+14 will then wire both together.
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked.
data.title: As a developer, arbiter output is enriched with cross_reviewer_agreement (4-val), cross_cycle_pattern (7-val), and impact_class (8-val floor enforced by BLOCK gate)
